units.characteristics: intellectual humility before the unknowable God
units.gist: CORNERSTONE - Agur's weariness and confession - 'I am weary, O God... I am too stupid to be a man... I have not learned wisdom, nor have knowledge of the Holy One'; the seeker's self-emptying before God's unsearchable greatness

units.characteristics: contentment - the prayer for the middle; how wealth/want endanger the heart
units.gist: CORNERSTONE - 'give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with the food that is needful... lest I be FULL and DENY you... or POOR and STEAL and profane your name' - the self-knowledge that both excess and lack imperil fidelity

units.characteristics: self-deception - clean in one's own eyes; lofty eyes
units.gist: 'there are those who are clean in their own eyes but are not washed of their filth'; 'how lofty are their eyes' (self-deception + pride, w/ 20:9, 16:2)

'the leech has two daughters: Give and Give'; the four never-satisfied (Sheol, the barren womb, the parched land, the fire) - the insatiable, and the adulteress who 'wipes her mouth: I have done no wrong' (seared conscience)

units.characteristics: self-restraint - the hand on the mouth
units.gist: 'if you have been foolish, exalting yourself, or devising evil, put your hand on your mouth; pressing anger produces strife' (checking the self before it spills)

units.characteristics: self-mastery and advocacy - the king's charge
units.gist: the mother's charge to Lemuel - do not give strength to women/wine (self-mastery lest judgment be perverted); 'open your mouth for the mute... defend the rights of the poor and needy' (the self turned to the voiceless)

units.characteristics: the fear-of-the-LORD woman - trust, inner strength, fearless hope, wise-kind speech
units.gist: CORNERSTONE + book-close - the excellent wife: 'the heart of her husband TRUSTS in her'; 'she dresses herself with STRENGTH... strength and dignity are her clothing, and she LAUGHS at the time to come' (fearless hope); 'she opens her mouth with wisdom, the teaching of KINDNESS on her tongue'; and the cap - 'charm is deceitful and beauty is vain, but a woman who FEARS THE LORD is to be praised' (fear-of-the-LORD as the true worth, bookending 1:7)
